chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi: Regarding
a man who pledges an item with another man, and it is damaged or lost, he said: 'He returns with his money upon him (the pledgee).'

key_terms.يَرْجِعُ بِمَالِهِ عَلَيْهِ: he returns with his money upon him (the debt remains due)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the debt if the pledged collateral is lost or damaged?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *qabd* (possession) in pledge contracts, establishing that the pledgee bears the risk of loss for the collateral while it is in their custody. It underscores the Shia juristic view that the debt remains due regardless of the asset's condition, reflecting the practical need for security in commercial transactions during the early Islamic period. This ruling aligns with the broader fiqh concept that possession entails responsibility for preservation unless negligence is proven.
